newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says ready for official talks with China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says ready for official talks with China.

text.p: Taiwan said on Friday it was ready for official talks with rival China, but only if Beijing accepted the island's definition of "China".

"If the Chinese communists can accept our definition of China, the two sides of the Taiwan Strait can hold talks at any time," Kao Koong-liang, vice chairman of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, was quoted as saying by the Central News Agency.
"Not only our council will take part in the talks, but also the defence ministry and security authorities will send representatives for the talks," the state-funded agency quoted Kao as saying.
Kao said that for the sides to conduct dialogue, Beijing must accept Nationalist-ruled Taiwan's definition of China which he said was that "Taiwan and (the) mainland are two (equal) parts of China".
Taipei claims Taiwan and China are two equal political entities ruled by two governments. But Beijing says Taiwan is a renegade province of China that falls under its sovereignty.
Beijing also says its People's Republic of China government is the legitimate ruler of all China.
Taiwan has banned official contacts with China since they were split after a civil war in 1949. Taipei set up a semi-official body in 1991 to represent the government in talks with the mainland.
But those talks were suspended in 1995 after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui visited the United States, a trip seen by an outraged Beijing as a plot to promote Taiwan independence.
Beijing, which regards Taiwan as a rebel-held province subject to eventual unification with mainland China, threatens to attack the island if it declares independence.
